question: What is an advantage of streaming telemetry over SNMP?
options: on-change traps sent to a receiver
periodic polling of the device status
theory: Traditional SNMP relies on a pull model where a management station periodically polls devices (often every 5–10 minutes), which doesn't scale to many collectors and can't give near-real-time visibility. Streaming telemetry inverts this: the device proactively pushes structured data (JSON/GPB) to a subscribed collector at a configured cadence, so operators get continuous, low-latency updates instead of stale polled snapshots. This push-based subscription model is the key advantage streaming telemetry has over SNMP polling. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — Streaming Telemetry)
